mainTopic: The צומת הגידין (its strands and how much cutting makes a טרפה), and a broken leg bone: where the break is, and how much skin and flesh must still cover it
overview: The גמרא finishes defining the צומת הגידין, the bundle of sinews in the thigh. In an animal it has three strands, one thick and two thin. Two versions disagree on whether cutting the thick one or the two thin ones makes the animal a טרפה. In birds there are sixteen strands, and cutting even one makes it a טרפה. רב and שמואל then argue over how much must be cut, and the גמרא gives two versions of their exchange, compared with רבנאי's report of שמואל. Next comes the משנה's broken leg bone. רב says a break above the ארכובה with most of the flesh gone makes the animal a טרפה. שמואל says only the limb is forbidden. After a back-and-forth, the ruling from ארץ ישראל follows רב, and we learn that שמואל himself took back his view. The amud ends with a bone that broke and came out of the body. The גמרא discusses how much must stay covered and whether skin counts like flesh. It then starts a case of soft sinews before רבה, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The sinews count once they look clear, even before they turn white
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי says the area of the convergence of sinews starts as soon as the sinews look clear and glassy, even if they are not fully white yet.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר רב אשי said: Once the sinews look clear, even though they are not white, they already count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an earlier discussion about where along the leg the צומת הגידין starts. מר בר רב אשי gives his opinion on where it begins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the measure was the spot where the sinews turn white. מר בר רב אשי moves the starting point earlier, to where they first start to look clear. That makes the area bigger, so a cut a little higher up the leg can already count as a cut in the צומת הגידין.

keyTerms.meaning: They look clear or glassy (from the word for glass)

phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi said:
Once they look clear,
phrases.notes: "They" are the thigh sinews. The word comes from the Aramaic for glass, so picture them starting to look see-through.

phrases.english: even though they are not white.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר כֵּיוָן דְּזִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion (before this section) about where the צומת הגידין begins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The צומת הגידין begins where the sinews first look clear, even before they are white.

steps.title: Three strands: losing either the bulk or the count makes it a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: אמימר in the name of רב זביד: there are three strands, one thick and two thin. If the thick one is cut, most of the bulk is gone. If the two thin ones are cut, most of the count is gone. Either way it is a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said in the name of רב זביד: There are three strands, one thick and two thin. If the thick one is cut, most of the structure is gone. If the thin ones are cut, most of the number is gone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains what the צומת הגידין is made of: three strands. It then rules on what happens when some of them are cut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to measure 'most': by size (בנין) or by how many (מנין). The thick strand is bigger than the two thin ones put together, so cutting it removes most of the size. Cutting the two thin ones removes two out of three, which is most of the count. This version is strict: losing a majority in either way makes the animal a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: Most of the structure, measured by size
Most of the number, measured by count

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two kinds of 'most' apart. בנין means size: the one thick strand outweighs the other two. מנין means count: two strands out of three.

phrases.english: Ameimar said in the name of Rav Zevid:
There are three strands,
one thick and two thin.
If the thick one was cut,
most of the structure is gone;
phrases.notes: The thick strand is bigger than the other two together, so by size most of it is gone.

phrases.english: if the thin ones were cut,
most of the number is gone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַמֵּימָר מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב זְבִיד תְּלָתָא חוּטֵי הָווּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from where the צומת הגידין starts to what it is made of and how much damage makes it a טרפה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cutting the thick strand, or the two thin strands, makes the animal a טרפה, because either most of the size or most of the count is gone.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up the idea of two ways to measure a majority, which the next step turns around in the lenient direction.

steps.title: The lenient version: something always remains
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי teaches the same cases leniently. If the thick strand is cut, most of the count is still there. If the thin ones are cut, most of the size is still there. So it is not a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר רב אשי teaches it leniently: If the thick one is cut, most of the number is still there. If the thin ones are cut, most of the structure is still there.
steps.whatsHappening: מר בר רב אשי takes the very same two cases and reaches the opposite result. In his version the animal is kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב זביד looks at what was lost; מר בר רב אשי looks at what is left. Cutting the thick strand leaves two of the three strands, which is most of the count. Cutting the thin ones leaves the thick strand, which is most of the size. As long as one kind of majority is still there, the animal is not a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: Teaches it as (gives his version of the teaching)

steps.whatToRemember: Strict version (רב זביד): losing either kind of majority makes it a טרפה. Lenient version (מר בר רב אשי): keeping either kind of majority keeps it kosher.

phrases.aramaic: מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי מַתְנֵי לְקוּלָּא:
phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi teaches it leniently:
If the thick one was cut,
there is still most of the number;
if the thin ones were cut,
there is still most of the structure.
phrases.notes: The גמרא leaves the ruling unsaid, but the point is that in both cases the animal is not a טרפה.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי מַתְנֵי לְקוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a rival version of step 2, with the same cases and the opposite outcome.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If either kind of majority (count or size) remains, the animal is not a טרפה.

steps.title: Birds have sixteen strands, and cutting even one makes a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: In birds the צומת הגידין has sixteen strands, and if even one of them is cut the bird is a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: In birds there are sixteen strands. If one of them is cut, it is a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns from animals to birds. It gives a different count and a much stricter rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For animals, the question was about a majority of three strands. For birds, there is no talk of a majority at all: losing a single strand out of sixteen is enough to make it a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal or bird with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat

phrases.english: In birds there are sixteen strands;
if one of them was cut, it is a tereifa.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעוֹפוֹת שִׁיתְּסַר חוּטֵי הָווּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares birds with the three-strand structure in animals from steps 2 and 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bird's צומת הגידין has sixteen strands, and cutting even one makes it a טרפה.

steps.title: A story: fifteen strands that turned out to be sixteen
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי tells how his father, רב אשי, checked a bird and found only fifteen strands. One strand looked different, and when he split it, it turned out to be two.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר רב אשי said: I was standing before Father, and they brought him a bird. He checked it and found fifteen strands. One looked different from the others; he split it and found it was two.
steps.whatsHappening: מר בר רב אשי tells a real case that backs up the count of sixteen strands in a bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first the bird seemed to have only fifteen strands, which would go against the rule of sixteen. Looking closer showed that one strand was really two joined together. So the count of sixteen holds, and anyone checking a bird should look carefully for a strand that might be doubled.

keyTerms.meaning: He split it or pulled it apart

phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi said:
I was standing before Father,
phrases.notes: His father is רב אשי.

phrases.english: and they brought a bird before him,
and he checked and found fifteen in it.
There was one that was different from the others;
he split it apart and found two.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲוָה קָאֵימְנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּאַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the count of sixteen from step 4 with a real case.
steps.raayaObject: That a bird's צומת הגידין has sixteen strands.
steps.raayaSupportSource: An eyewitness case: רב אשי checked a bird, found fifteen strands, and discovered that one of them was really two.

steps.title: רב: cutting most of just one strand makes it a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: when the חכמים said that cutting 'most' of the צומת הגידין makes it a טרפה, they meant most of just one of its strands.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: The צומת הגידין that the חכמים spoke about is when most of it is cut. What does 'most of it' mean? Most of one of the strands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to animals. רב explains what 'most' means in the rule about cutting the צומת הגידין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think 'most' means most of the whole bundle. רב says it means most of a single strand. That is a very strict reading: even partial damage to one strand makes the animal a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: The convergence of sinews in the thigh

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
The convergence of sinews that they spoke of is when most of it is cut;
What is 'most of it'? Most of one of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב צוֹמֶת הַגִּידִין שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּרוּבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back from birds to the animal's three strands and defines 'most'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cutting most of even one strand of the צומת הגידין makes the animal a טרפה.

steps.title: שמואל: even if one strand is fully cut, two still remain
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה reports that when he said רב's ruling before שמואל, שמואל objected: there are three strands, so even if one is cut completely, two are still left.
steps.simpleTranslation: When I said this before שמואל, he said to me: There are three strands. When one of them is cut completely, two are still there.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה tells how שמואל pushed back against רב's strict ruling from the step before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said that cutting most of one strand is enough for a טרפה. שמואל points out that even a strand cut all the way through still leaves two out of three, which is a majority. So partial damage to one strand should certainly not make the animal a טרפה.
steps.whatToRemember: רב: cutting most of one strand makes it a טרפה. שמואל: even a whole strand cut still leaves two of three, so the animal is still kosher.

phrases.english: When I said it before Shmuel,
phrases.notes: "I" is רב יהודה, telling what happened when he repeated רב's ruling.

phrases.english: he said to me: Now, there are three;
when one of them is cut completely,
there are still two.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אַמְרִיתַהּ קַמֵּיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר לִי מִכְּדֵי תְּלָתָא הָווּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's definition of 'most' from step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that cutting most of one strand makes the animal a טרפה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Out of three strands, cutting even one completely leaves two, which is a majority. So damage to part of one strand cannot be what makes it a טרפה.

steps.title: Inference from שמואל's objection: two strands must remain
steps.stepSummary: From שמואל's words 'two are still left,' the גמרא infers that if two strands are not left, the animal is not kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: The only reason it is kosher is that two strands are left. If two are not left, it is not kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads closely into שמואל's objection from step 7. It notices that his reason for calling the animal kosher was that two whole strands were left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said that if one strand is cut, two are still left, so the animal is kosher. The גמרא infers the flip side. If two strands are cut and only one is left, the animal is a טרפה, even though one strand is still whole. This inference sets up the clash in the next step.

phrases.english: The reason is that there are two,
phrases.notes: Two whole strands of the צומת הגידין are left, as שמואל said in step 7.

phrases.english: but if there are not two – no.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּאִיכָּא תְּרֵי, הָא לֵיכָּא תְּרֵי – לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an implication from the wording of שמואל's objection in step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In this version, שמואל holds that two whole strands must remain. If only one remains, the animal is a טרפה.

steps.title: This version clashes with רבנאי's report of שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that this inference disagrees with רבנאי, who quoted שמואל as saying that even a thread-thin remnant is enough to keep the animal kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: This disagrees with רבנאי, who said in שמואל's name: with the צומת הגידין, even if only a piece as thin as the string of a cloak is left, the animal is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notes that, under this version, שמואל's view conflicts with another report of his opinion, the one given by רבנאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 inferred that one whole strand left is not enough. רבנאי, however, reports that שמואל said even a tiny remnant, as thin as a cloak string, keeps the animal kosher. So the two reports of שמואל point in opposite directions. The גמרא simply records this disagreement here.

keyTerms.meaning: It disagrees (two opinions or reports conflict)
The place where the sinews of the leg come together
The thin string used to close the neckline of a cloak

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rabbenai,
for Rabbenai said that Shmuel said:
The convergence of sinews,
even if nothing remains of it
except as much as the string of a cloak – it is kosher.
phrases.notes: In this version, he means just one strand is left, and it is very thin.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּפְלִיגָא דְּרַבְנַאי, דְּאָמַר רַבְנַאי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the inference from step 8 against a conflicting report of שמואל's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבנאי in the name of שמואל: even a thread-thin remnant of the צומת הגידין keeps the animal kosher.
steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions here come from שמואל. The disagreement is between two different reports of what שמואל held, not between two different sages.

steps.title: Second version: 'most' means most of each strand
steps.stepSummary: A different version of רב יהודה's report: 'most' of the צומת הגידין means most of every single strand.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: What does 'most of it' mean? Most of each and every strand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a second version of the whole exchange between רב יהודה and שמואל. This time רב's meaning of 'most' is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version (step 6), 'most' meant most of just one strand. Here it means most of each of the three strands. That is a much harder standard to meet before the animal becomes a טרפה.

phrases.english: And some say:
What is "most of it"?
Most of each and every one.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: מַאי רוּבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second version of רב's statement from step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under this version, the animal becomes a טרפה only if most of each strand is cut.

steps.title: שמואל objects: a third of each strand is enough
steps.stepSummary: In this second version, שמואל objects that since there are three strands, a third left in each is enough to keep the animal kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: When I said this before שמואל, he said to me: After all, there are three strands. There is a third left of each and every one.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה tells how שמואל pushed back on the second version of רב's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version רב says the animal is a טרפה once most of each strand is cut. שמואל answers that since there are three strands, a third left of each one is enough, so a majority of each strand does not need to remain. That makes him more lenient than רב.

phrases.english: When I said it before Shmuel,
phrases.notes: The speaker is רב יהודה, the same person as in step 7.

phrases.english: he said to me:
After all, there are three,
there is a third of each and every one.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אַמְרִיתַהּ קַמֵּיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל, אָמַר לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: שמואל challenges the second version of רב's rule from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that most of each strand must be cut (in the second version)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since there are three strands, a third remaining in each one is enough, so there is no need for a majority of each strand to remain.

steps.title: This version matches רבנאי's report
steps.stepSummary: In the second version, שמואל's view supports רבנאי's report that even a thread-thin remnant keeps the animal kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רבנאי, who said in שמואל's name: with the צומת הגידין the חכמים spoke of, even if only a piece as thin as a cloak string is left, the animal is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that, in the second version, the two reports of שמואל now agree with each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version there was a clash with רבנאי (step 9). Now שמואל is lenient: even when most of each strand is cut, the small remnants of all three together are enough. That fits רבנאי's report, read here as a thin remnant of each of the three strands. So the second version removes the clash.
steps.whatToRemember: First version: שמואל needs two whole strands, which clashes with רבנאי. Second version: שמואל is satisfied with a small part of each strand, which supports רבנאי.

phrases.english: This supports Rabbenai,
for Rabbenai said that Shmuel said:
The convergence of sinews that they spoke of,
even if nothing remains of it
except as much as the string of a cloak – it is kosher.
phrases.notes: Here he means a thin piece is left of each of the three strands.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבְנַאי, דְּאָמַר רַבְנַאי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that שמואל's objection in step 11 fits רבנאי's report.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's view in the second version
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבנאי's report in the name of שמואל about the cloak string
steps.whyThisMatters: The choice between the two versions decides how much of the צומת הגידין must remain for the animal to stay kosher.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: if the bone was broken
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to a new line of the משנה about a broken leg bone.
steps.simpleTranslation: "If the bone was broken, etc."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה to begin a new topic. It is setting up רב's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that if a bone breaks and most of the surrounding flesh is intact, the שחיטה permits the limb, and if not, it does not. The quote here is just the opening words, and the discussion is about to follow.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc. (the rest of the משנה's words)

phrases.english: "If the bone was broken, etc."
phrases.notes: The משנה continues: if most of the flesh is intact, the שחיטה permits the limb; if not, it does not.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִשְׁבַּר הָעֶצֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the צומת הגידין topic and opens a new line of the משנה.

steps.title: רב: above or below the knee joint makes a difference
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that if the break is above the ארכובה and most of the flesh is gone, both the animal and the limb are forbidden. If the break is below it, only the limb is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: If the break is above the knee joint and most of the flesh is intact, both the animal and the limb are permitted. If not, both are forbidden. If the break is below the knee joint and most of the flesh is intact, both are permitted. If not, the limb is forbidden but the animal is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains the משנה's case of a broken bone by splitting it into two places: above the ארכובה and below it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If most of the flesh is intact, everything is permitted in both places. If most of the flesh is gone, the place matters. Above the ארכובה, the animal becomes a טרפה, so the animal and the limb are both forbidden. Below the ארכובה, the animal is not a טרפה, but the dangling limb is not made permitted by the שחיטה, so only the limb is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The knee joint of the leg
Most of the flesh is intact
This and that (the animal and the limb)

steps.whatToRemember: Most flesh intact: everything is permitted. Most flesh gone above the ארכובה: animal and limb are both forbidden. Most flesh gone below the ארכובה: only the limb is forbidden.
steps.confusionAlert: 'זה וזה' means the animal and the broken limb. It does not mean two different animals.

phrases.english: Rav said:
Above the knee joint,
if most of the flesh is intact –
both this and that are permitted,
phrases.notes: 'This and that' means the animal and the broken limb.

phrases.english: and if not – both this and that are forbidden.
Below the knee joint,
if most of the flesh is intact –
both this and that are permitted,

phrases.aramaic: אִם לָאו – אֵבֶר אָסוּר וּבְהֵמָה מוּתֶּרֶת.
phrases.english: if not – the limb is forbidden and the animal is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: לְמַעְלָה מִן הָאַרְכּוּבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the משנה line quoted in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A break above the ארכובה with most of the flesh gone forbids both the animal and the limb. A break below it forbids only the limb.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the line between a break that makes the whole animal a טרפה and one that only affects the limb itself.

steps.title: שמואל's ruling: the animal stays kosher either way
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that the place of the break makes no difference. If most of the flesh is intact, both the limb and the animal are permitted. If not, only the limb is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: whether the break is above or below the ארכובה, if most of the flesh is still there, both are permitted. If not, the limb is forbidden and the animal is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings שמואל's opinion, which disagrees with רב's ruling from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said that a break above the ארכובה with most of the flesh gone makes the whole animal forbidden. שמואל says the place of the break does not matter. A missing majority of flesh only forbids the limb itself, and the animal stays kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: Most of the flesh around the break is still intact
Above or below (the ארכובה, the leg joint)
Both this and that are permitted

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
whether above or below,
phrases.notes: He means above or below the ארכובה, the joint רב was talking about.

phrases.english: if most of the flesh is intact,
this and that are permitted,
phrases.notes: "This and that" means the limb and the animal.

phrases.english: if not, the limb is forbidden,
and the animal is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רב's ruling in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whether the break is above or below the ארכובה, a missing majority of flesh forbids only the limb. The animal is permitted.

steps.title: רב נחמן worries that people will be misled
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן objects to שמואל: people will see a limb of the animal thrown in the garbage while the animal is eaten, and they will draw the wrong conclusion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן challenged שמואל: People will say, "A limb from it lies in the garbage, and the animal is permitted?"
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן attacks שמואל's ruling. He is not using a source. He is worried about how it will look to people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under שמואל, the leg gets thrown out and the animal is eaten. רב נחמן fears people will wrongly conclude that the animal is kosher even when that leg is fully cut off.

keyTerms.meaning: Challenged it; raised a strong objection
People will say (a concern about how things look)

phrases.english: Rav Nachman challenged Shmuel:
People will say: "A limb from it lies in the garbage
and it is permitted?"

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב נַחְמָן לִשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's ruling from step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that the animal is permitted while the limb is forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Throwing out a limb while eating the animal looks strange, and people may come to permit an animal even when its leg is truly cut off.

steps.title: The same worry applies to רב too
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר רב הונא points out to רב נחמן that רב also has this exact situation, when the break is below the ארכובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר רב הונא said to רב נחמן: According to רב too, people will say, "A limb from it lies in the garbage, and the animal is permitted!"
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר רב הונא pushes back on רב נחמן's objection. He shows that it proves too much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב also rules, for a break below the ארכובה, that the limb is forbidden and the animal is permitted. So if רב נחמן's worry were real, it would be a problem for רב as well, not just for שמואל.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר רַב הוּנָא לְרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Rav Huna said to Rav Nachman:
According to Rav too, they will say:
phrases.notes: He means רב's case of a break below the ארכובה from step 14.

phrases.english: "A limb from it lies in the garbage
and it is permitted!"

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר רַב הוּנָא לְרַב נַחְמָן לְרַב נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Counters רב נחמן's objection in step 16 by showing that it also applies to רב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב also permits the animal while forbidding the limb (below the ארכובה), so the worry cannot be used to reject שמואל alone.

steps.title: רב נחמן explains which limb he meant
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן clarifies that his worry is about a limb the animal needs in order to live. Only שמואל has that problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what I meant. A limb that the animal lives by is lying in the garbage, and the animal is permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רב אחא by explaining exactly what he meant. His worry applies to שמואל and not to רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the leg is fully cut off above the ארכובה, the animal becomes a טרפה. If it is cut off below, the animal stays kosher. רב only permits the animal in the case below, where nobody would be misled. שמואל also permits it above, and there people might confuse a broken leg with a cut-off one and permit a real טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what I meant to say
That the animal lives by (its loss would make the animal a טרפה)
An animal with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat even after שחיטה

steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is not changing his worry into a new one. He is narrowing it: the only limb that matters is one whose loss would make the animal a טרפה.

phrases.english: He said to him: This is what I meant:
A limb that it lives by
lies in the garbage, and it is permitted?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָכִי קָאָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אחא's counter-challenge in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying and narrowing the original objection
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן's worry seemed to cover any forbidden limb of a permitted animal, which would include רב's case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The worry only covers a limb whose loss would make the animal a טרפה (above the ארכובה), and only שמואל permits the animal there.

steps.title: The ruling from ארץ ישראל goes back and forth, then follows רב
steps.stepSummary: A ruling was sent from ארץ ישראל. It first followed רב, then שמואל, and finally רב again. It added that the limb itself makes things טמא when carried.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent from there: The הלכה follows רב. Then they sent again: it follows שמואל. Then they sent again: it follows רב, and the limb itself makes things טמא through carrying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the dispute with a ruling from the sages of ארץ ישראל. After going back and forth, the final word follows רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the last message follows רב, a break above the ארכובה with most of the flesh gone makes the animal a טרפה. The last message also adds that the שחיטה does not purify the broken limb. It carries טומאה through carrying, like a limb from a living animal.

keyTerms.meaning: They sent from there (from ארץ ישראל)
Again; then they changed and sent again
Makes a person טמא when he carries it
A limb from a living animal, which carries טומאה

steps.whatToRemember: The final הלכה follows רב. A break above the ארכובה with most of the flesh gone makes the animal a טרפה. A break below it forbids only the limb. The limb itself makes things טמא through carrying.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical ruling for the broken-leg case in the משנה. It also teaches that שחיטה does not purify the broken limb.

phrases.english: They sent from there:
phrases.notes: "There" means ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: The halacha follows Rav,
they sent again: it follows Shmuel,
they sent again: it follows Rav,
and the limb itself makes things impure through carrying.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַחוּ מִתָּם הִלְכְתָא כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the רב/שמואל dispute that steps 15 to 18 were discussing.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רב, and the broken limb itself makes things טמא through carrying.

steps.title: רב חסדא challenges the ruling from רבי מאיר's words about a dangling limb
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא quotes רבי מאיר from an earlier ברייתא. רבי מאיר takes it for granted that שחיטה makes a dangling limb טהור. That clashes with the ruling that the limb itself is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא raised an objection. רבי מאיר said: No! Slaughtering a טרפה makes the animal טהור, and also the limb dangling from it. But that is something that is part of the animal's own body. Should it also make the fetus's limb טהור, when the fetus is not part of the mother's body?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא attacks the ruling from Step 19 that the dangling limb itself makes things טמא. He uses words of רבי מאיר that assume the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר uses a 'this is not like that' argument. Along the way he states as obvious that שחיטה makes a dangling limb טהור. If שחיטה makes the limb טהור, it cannot be the kind of limb that makes things טמא when carried.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal defect. It may not be eaten even after שחיטה.
A limb that is partly cut off but still hangs from the animal.
Made it טהור, so it no longer has the טומאה of a dead animal (נבלה).
The fetus inside the mother animal.

steps.confusionAlert: רב חסדא is not quoting רבי מאיר's main point, which is about the fetus. He is using what רבי מאיר takes for granted along the way: that the dangling limb becomes טהור.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא, אִם טִיהֲרָה שְׁחִיטַת טְרֵפָה אוֹתָהּ
phrases.english: No, if the slaughter of a tereifa purified it
phrases.notes: These are רבי מאיר's words from a ברייתא quoted earlier on 73a, about a fetus that stuck a limb out of the womb.

phrases.english: and the limb dangling from it
that is something that is part of its body
should it purify the fetus,
phrases.notes: He means the fetus's limb that came out of the womb.

phrases.english: something that is not part of its body?

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the last part of the ruling from ארץ ישראל: that the dangling limb itself makes things טמא when carried.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the dangling limb itself is טמא like a limb from a living animal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר assumes that שחיטה makes a dangling limb טהור. So the limb is treated as part of a slaughtered animal, not as a limb from a living animal that carries its own טומאה.

steps.title: רבה suggests a stronger challenge from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבה tells רב חסדא he does not need to dig up a ברייתא. A משנה shows that a dangling limb can be made able to become טמא by the animal's blood. That only makes sense if the limb is not already טמא on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to him: Why go searching for refutations? Raise your objection from a משנה! The משנה says that once the animal is slaughtered, the dangling parts are made able to receive טומאה by its blood. That is רבי מאיר's view. רבי שמעון says they are not made able to receive טומאה that way.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה agrees with רב חסדא's goal but points him to a better source, a משנה that everyone knows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something that is already a source of טומאה does not need הכשר. If the dangling limb needs הכשר through the blood, it must not be טמא on its own. Both רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון seem to treat it this way, so the challenge is stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: They were made able to receive food טומאה (הכשר).
Food getting wet with one of seven liquids, such as blood, which makes it able to become טמא.

phrases.english: Rabba said to him:
Why do you need to go searching for refutations?
Raise an objection from the Mishnah!
If the animal was slaughtered, they were made susceptible by its blood,
phrases.notes: 'They' means the dangling limb and flesh. This משנה is later in this מסכת, on 127b.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Shimon says: They were not made susceptible.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַדּוֹרֵי אַפִּירְכֵי לְמָה לָךְ? אוֹתֵיב מִמַּתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a stronger source for the same challenge רב חסדא raised.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the dangling limb itself is טמא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the dangling limb needs הכשר, it cannot already be a source of טומאה.

steps.title: רב חסדא explains why the משנה is not a strong challenge
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that the משנה can be pushed aside, the same way it was pushed aside earlier. That is why he chose the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The משנה can be pushed aside, the way we already pushed it aside.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא explains to רבה why he did not use the משנה. It already has a known answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, on 73a, the גמרא said the argument in the משנה is only about dangling flesh, not a dangling limb. So the משנה proves nothing about a limb. רבי מאיר's words in the ברייתא clearly mention the limb, so that challenge is stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: To push aside, to reject a proof.
As we already pushed it aside.

phrases.english: He said to him:
The Mishnah can be pushed aside,
as we already pushed it aside.
phrases.notes: Back on 73a, the גמרא said the משנה is talking about dangling flesh, not a dangling limb.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין אִיכָּא לְדַחוֹיֵי, כִּדְדָחֵינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבה's suggested source as weaker than the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the משנה. רב חסדא's own challenge from the ברייתא still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה can be read as talking about dangling flesh only, so it says nothing about a limb.
steps.whyThisMatters: רב חסדא's challenge from the ברייתא is left without an answer here. This shows the limb part of the ruling is under real pressure.

steps.title: רבי זירא hears רב's ruling taught in ארץ ישראל and says it was taught in בבל too
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא moves to ארץ ישראל and finds רב ירמיה teaching רב's ruling about a break above the ארכובה. רבי זירא praises him and says אריוך taught the same in בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי זירא went up to ארץ ישראל, he found רב ירמיה sitting and teaching this הלכה. He told him: Well said! אריוך explained it the same way in בבל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that supports רב's view. It also sets up the next question: who is אריוך?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הלכה is רב's ruling. If the break is above the ארכובה and most of the flesh is not intact, the animal is a טרפה. רבי זירא says the same thing was taught in בבל, which seems to show that בבל agrees too.

keyTerms.meaning: Went up, here meaning moved to ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: When Rabbi Zeira went up to Eretz Yisrael,
he found Rav Yirmeya
sitting and saying this halacha.
phrases.notes: 'This הלכה' is רב's ruling about a bone broken above the ארכובה.

phrases.english: He said to him: Well said,
and Aryokh explained it the same way in Bavel.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי סָלֵיק רַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the main argument between רב and שמואל about where the break is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב's ruling was taught in ארץ ישראל, and the same ruling was said to have been taught by אריוך in בבל.

steps.title: Who is אריוך? שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who אריוך is. The answer is שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is אריוך? It is שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to explain the nickname אריוך. It is setting up the next difficulty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing that אריוך is שמואל matters a lot. It means שמואל taught רב's ruling. That clashes with Step 15, where שמואל disagreed.

keyTerms.meaning: Babylonia, where שמואל lived and taught.

phrases.english: Who is Aryokh?
Shmuel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַרְיוֹךְ מַנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains who the person named in the story is.

steps.title: But שמואל disagrees with רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out the problem. שמואל disagreed with רב, so how could he teach רב's ruling?
steps.simpleTranslation: But he clearly disagrees!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a contradiction between the story and שמואל's own view in Step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 15, שמואל said the place of the break makes no difference. Here he is said to have taught רב's view, which does depend on the place of the break. Both cannot be true unless something changed.

keyTerms.meaning: He clearly disagrees. The doubled verb adds emphasis.

phrases.english: But he clearly disagrees!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מִיפְלָג פְּלִיג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer that אריוך is שמואל to point out a contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The report that שמואל taught רב's ruling.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל is on record (Step 15) disagreeing with רב on this exact point.

steps.title: שמואל took back his view and agreed with רב
steps.stepSummary: The answer: שמואל changed his mind and accepted רב's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל took back his view in favor of רב's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the contradiction. שמואל changed his opinion and came over to רב's side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reports are true, but at different times. שמואל first disagreed and later agreed with רב. This fits the final ruling from ארץ ישראל (Step 19), which followed רב.

keyTerms.meaning: He took back his view, he changed his mind.
Toward him, over to his side.

steps.whatToRemember: In the end, רב and שמואל agree. A break above the ארכובה, with most of the flesh not intact, makes the animal a טרפה.

phrases.english: Shmuel took back his view
in favor of Rav's.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר בֵּיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל לְגַבֵּיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Change of view over time: שמואל took back his earlier opinion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought שמואל still held that the place of the break makes no difference.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל later agreed with רב, so the report from בבל is correct.
steps.whyThisMatters: This settles the main argument of the sugya in favor of רב, matching the final ruling sent from ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: A broken bone that comes out: is it covered?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that a bone that broke and came out is permitted only if skin and flesh cover most of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: if the bone broke and came out, then if skin and flesh cover most of it, the animal is permitted. If not, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a new rule about a broken bone that pokes out of the body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deciding factor is coverage. If skin and flesh still cover most of the bone, the animal is כשר. If they do not, it is forbidden. The rest of the sugya will explain what 'most' means and how skin counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Came out (the bone sticks out of the body)

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the base text for everything that follows in this section.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If the bone broke and came out,

phrases.aramaic: אִם עוֹר וּבָשָׂר חוֹפִין אֶת רוּבּוֹ – מוּתָּר,
phrases.english: if skin and flesh cover most of it, it is permitted;
if not, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: נִשְׁבַּר הָעֶצֶם וְיָצָא לַחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: a bone that broke and came out through the skin.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A broken bone that came out is permitted only if skin and flesh cover most of it.

steps.title: How much counts as most of the bone?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'most of the bone' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much is 'most of it'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the ברייתא's word 'most'. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bone has a length, a thickness and a distance around it. The ברייתא did not say which one is measured, so the גמרא asks.

phrases.english: And how much is "most of it"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכַמָּה רוּבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the measurement behind the word 'most' in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which part of the bone must be mostly covered.

steps.title: Two versions: thickness or circumference
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports רבי יוחנן's answer in two versions: most of the bone's thickness, or most of its circumference.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: most of its thickness. Some say he said: most of its circumference.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question, but the answer came down in two versions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One version says to measure across the bone, its thickness. The other version says to measure around it, its circumference. We do not know for sure which one רבי יוחנן said.

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came,
he said that Rabbi Yochanan said: most of its thickness;
and some say: most of its circumference.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Most of the thickness, or in another version, most of the circumference.

steps.title: We require both measurements
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that since we are unsure, the bone must be covered by most of its thickness and also by most of its circumference.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: therefore, we need most of its thickness, and we need most of its circumference.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא settles the doubt from the last step by being strict on both sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We do not know which version of רבי יוחנן is correct. So we require the bone to be mostly covered both ways, and only then is the animal כשר.
steps.whatToRemember: A protruding bone must be covered across most of its thickness AND most of its circumference.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: Therefore,
we need most of its thickness,
and we need most of its circumference.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הִלְכָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the two versions given in step 29.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both measurements are required, to be safe.

steps.title: Skin counts just like flesh
steps.stepSummary: עולא reports in רבי יוחנן's name that skin is treated like flesh for covering the bone.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: skin is like flesh.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement: עולא says that skin alone can do the job of flesh in covering the bone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא spoke of 'skin and flesh'. עולא's teaching means that even if only skin covers most of the bone, the animal is still permitted.

phrases.english: Ulla said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Skin is like flesh.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: עוֹר הֲרֵי הוּא כְּבָשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new question about the ברייתא: what role does skin play?
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Skin alone counts as covering, just like flesh.

steps.title: Shouldn't skin only join together with flesh?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן challenges עולא: the ברייתא says 'skin AND flesh', so skin should only count together with flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to עולא: Let the master say that skin joins together with flesh, since the ברייתא teaches 'skin and flesh'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן challenges עולא from the exact wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Skin and flesh' sounds like both are needed together. So רב נחמן argues that skin can only help flesh cover the bone, and skin alone is not enough. That is stricter than עולא's 'skin is like flesh'.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the master say (why not say instead...)

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to Ulla:
Let the master say that skin joins together with flesh,
since it teaches "skin and flesh"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְעוּלָּא: וְלֵימָא מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks עולא's statement in step 31.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's ruling that skin alone is like flesh.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's words 'skin and flesh' suggest that skin works only together with flesh.

steps.title: Our version reads 'skin or flesh'
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers that his version of the ברייתא says 'skin OR flesh'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We learned it as 'skin or flesh'.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא defends himself by pointing to a different wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the text says 'skin or flesh', then either one alone is enough. This fits עולא's ruling that skin alone counts like flesh.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנַן ״עוֹר אוֹ בָּשָׂר״ תָּנֵינַן.
phrases.english: He said to him: We learned "skin or flesh."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנַן ״עוֹר אוֹ בָּשָׂר״ תָּנֵינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב נחמן's challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא says 'skin and flesh', so both are needed together.
steps.terutzMaskana: The correct wording is 'skin or flesh', so skin alone is enough.

steps.title: Second version: skin joins with flesh
steps.stepSummary: A second version of עולא's report: רבי יוחנן said that skin joins together with flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: עולא said that רבי יוחנן said: skin joins together with flesh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of what עולא reported, and it is stricter than the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here skin cannot do the job alone. But together with flesh, it can help add up to covering most of the bone.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two versions. In the first, עולא says skin alone is enough. In this one, skin only helps together with flesh.

phrases.english: Some say: Ulla said
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: עוֹר מִצְטָרֵף לְבָשָׂר.
phrases.english: that Rabbi Yochanan said: Skin joins together with flesh.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי [אָמַר עוּלָּא], אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the first version of עולא's statement (step 31) with another version.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Skin and flesh together can add up to covering most of the bone.

steps.title: Shouldn't skin only finish off the flesh?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן suggests a stricter rule: skin only completes a coverage that is mostly flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to עולא: Let the master say that skin only completes the flesh, to be strict!
steps.whatsHappening: Again רב נחמן pushes עולא toward a stricter reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Joins together' could mean skin and flesh count equally. רב נחמן suggests that skin can only fill in a small missing part, so flesh must do most of the covering. That is a stricter rule.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to Ulla:

phrases.aramaic: וְלֵימָא מָר עוֹר מַשְׁלִים לְבָשָׂר לְחוּמְרָא!
phrases.english: Let the master say that skin completes the flesh, to be strict!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְעוּלָּא: וְלֵימָא מָר עוֹר מַשְׁלִים לְבָשָׂר לְחוּמְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second version of עולא's statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's second version, that skin joins equally with flesh.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It would be safer to say skin only completes a coverage that is mostly flesh.

steps.title: A real case: רבי יצחק's young bird
steps.stepSummary: עולא proves his ruling from a real case: רבי יוחנן declared כשר a young bird whose bone was covered by skin together with flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I know of a real case. There was a young bird in רבי יצחק's house, where skin joined with flesh to cover the bone. It came before רבי יוחנן, and he declared it כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers רב נחמן by pointing to a real-life ruling of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that case, skin and flesh together covered the bone, and רבי יוחנן said it was כשר. So עולא says skin really does join with flesh, not just fill in a small leftover part.

phrases.english: He said to him: I know of a real case,

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָהוּא בַּר גּוֹזָלָא דַּהֲוָה בֵּי רַבִּי יִצְחָק,
phrases.english: of a certain young bird that was in the house of Rabbi Yitzchak,
where it was a case of skin joining with flesh,
and it came before Rabbi Yochanan, and he declared it kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא עוֹבָדָא יָדַעְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב נחמן's suggestion with proof from a real case.
steps.raayaObject: That skin joins equally with flesh, as עולא reported.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's ruling that רבי יצחק's young bird was כשר.

steps.title: A young bird is different
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rejects the proof: a young bird has soft skin, so its skin is like flesh. That case does not teach us about other animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You are talking about a young bird? A young bird, whose skin is soft, is different.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן pushes aside עולא's proof by saying the case was special.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A young bird's skin is soft, almost like flesh, so of course it counts fully. That ruling does not prove that normal, tougher skin joins with flesh in other animals.
steps.whatToRemember: Proofs from a real case can be pushed aside if the case had something special about it. Here, it was the young bird's soft skin.

phrases.english: He said to him: You are talking about a young bird?
A young bird, which is soft, is different.
phrases.notes: 'Soft' refers to its skin. Because it is soft, it counts like flesh.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּר גּוֹזָלָא קָאָמְרַתְּ? בַּר גּוֹזָלָא דְּרַכִּיךְ שָׁאנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 36.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the young bird, not עולא's statement itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A young bird's skin is soft like flesh, so its case cannot teach us about normal skin.

steps.title: A case of soft sinews comes before רבה
steps.stepSummary: A case of soft sinews covering a bone comes to רבה, and he asks what there is to be concerned about.
steps.simpleTranslation: There were certain soft sinews that came before רבה. רבה said: What should we worry about with them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story: a case of soft sinews came to רבה for a ruling. רבה answers with a question that shows he leans toward being lenient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was about skin joining with flesh. Now a different material is in question: soft sinews. רבה's question 'what should we worry about?' means he sees no real reason to declare the animal טריפה, and he is about to explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: What should we be concerned about with them? A way of saying 'there is no real concern here'

steps.confusionAlert: רבה's question is not a real request for information. It is his way of saying the case is כשר, and he backs it up with reasons right after.

phrases.english: Those certain soft sinews
that came before Rabba,
Rabba said: For what should we be concerned about them?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנְהוּ גִּידִין רַכִּין דַּאֲתוֹ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the young-bird proof about skin was rejected, the גמרא brings a new real case, this time about soft sinews instead of skin.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה holds that there is no concern with soft sinews covering the bone. His reasons follow.

steps.title: רבה's first reason begins with a teaching of רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רבה gives his first reason, quoting רבי יוחנן about sinews that will eventually harden. The sentence continues beyond this section.
steps.simpleTranslation: First, because רבי יוחנן said: Sinews that will eventually become hard...
steps.whatsHappening: רבה starts listing his reasons for being lenient. His first reason is a teaching of רבי יוחנן about sinews that will later harden. The quote is only beginning here and finishes in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word חדא ('first') tells us רבה has more than one reason. He is building support from רבי יוחנן's teaching about sinews that will become hard later. What רבי יוחנן says about such sinews comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: First; one reason. It shows more reasons are coming
That will eventually harden; they are soft now but will become hard later

phrases.english: First, because Rabbi Yochanan said:
Sinews that will eventually harden

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲדָא, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: גִּידִין שֶׁסּוֹפָן לְהַקְשׁוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבה begins explaining his lenient question from the previous step by bringing his first supporting reason.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's lenient view that soft sinews covering the bone are no cause for concern
steps.raayaSupportSource: A teaching of רבי יוחנן about sinews that will eventually harden. It is cut off here and completed in the continuation.
